title: A Protocol for _Agrobacterium_-mediated Transformation of Cucumber \(_Cucumis sativus_ L.) from cotyledon explants
protocol: Reconstitute cucumber seeds using Cl₂ by adding 2 ml HCl to 15 ml NaClO in a sealed container.
Soak mature cucumber seeds in tap water for 2 hours at room temperature in a Petri dish.
Remove seed coats from seeds with forceps starting from the pointed end and then pushing aside the coat.
Sterilize 20-50 seeds for 30 seconds with 75% ethanol in a sterile Petri dish.
Drain ethanol and rinse seeds three times with sterile deionized water after shaking gently for 15 minutes in 3% sodium hypochlorite solution.
Place surface-sterilized seeds onto Petri plates containing seed germination medium, allowing 15-25 seeds per plate.
Germinate seeds in the dark at 28°C for 2 days.
Inoculate 2 ml of LB liquid medium with rifampicin and Kanamycin with a single Agrobacterium colony.
Culture inoculated medium at 28°C on a shaker at 200 rpm for 24 hours.
Subculture 200 μl of 2 ml culture into 50 ml LB liquid medium containing rifampicin and Kanamycin.
Culture at 28°C in a shaker at 200 rpm until OD600 reaches 0.6-0.8.
Spin the Agrobacterium culture down at 4000g or 5000g for 10 min at room temperature.
Remove the supernatant and rinse the pellet with 1 ml liquid MS medium.
Dilute the MS medium containing Agrobacterium to OD600=0.25 using MS liquid medium.
Pull seedlings out of the germination medium and place them in empty sterile Petri plates with a stack of sterile filter paper.
Cut the radicle first, then cut off 1/2-1/3 the end of cotyledon and remove the endopleura simultaneously.
Detach the upside cotyledon using a sterile scalpel.
Knock the hypocotyl to detach the downside cotyledon and growing point with sterile forceps and scalpel.
Collect detached cotyledons into MS liquid medium without Agrobacterium in a 50 ml sterile glass beaker.
Pour out the MS liquid medium without Agrobacterium.
Pour into MS liquid medium containing Agrobacterium (OD600=0.25) and shake gently.
Cover the sterile glass beaker with sterile culture container sealing film.
Put the beaker into the desiccator connected to a vacuum pump.
Apply two sessions of vacuum infiltration for 5 minutes each.
Leave explants in Agrobacterium medium for another 5 minutes.
Pour out the MS liquid medium containing Agrobacterium.
Place a sterile filter paper onto cocultivation medium and touch it exactly.
Transfer infected explants onto the filter paper with adaxial surface upward using forceps.
Allow about 20-35 explants per Petri dish plate.
Seal the Petri dish and incubate in darkness at 28°C for 2 days.
Transfer explants onto shooting medium containing 50 mg/ml kanamycin and 500 mg/ml carbenicillin.
Place 5-6 explants per Petri dish plate to allow growth.
Incubate under light (150 μmol m^-2^ s^-1^, 16 hours) at 25°C for 2-3 weeks.
Pull the explants out and place them in an empty sterile Petri plate with a stack of sterile filter paper.
Cut the shoots off using sterile forceps and scalpel.
Remove embryoids from the end part of the shoots.
Transfer shoots to 100 ml glass Erlenmeyer flasks containing rooting medium with kanamycin (50 mg/l) and carbenicillin (500 mg/l).
Incubate three to four shoots per flask under light (150 μmol m^-2^ s^-1^, 16 h) at 25°C for 1-2 weeks.
Take out no rooting plants after 1-2 weeks.
Recut unfolded leaves and the end part of the shoots using sterile forceps and tweezers.
Transfer shoots to new rooting medium.
Repeat recutting procedure one time per week in the next 2-3 weeks.
Place one to two shoots per glass Erlenmeyer flask.
Incubate under light (150 μmol m^-2^ s^-1^, 16 h) at 25°C for 2-4 weeks.
Incubate in dim light (10-50 μmol m^-2^ s^-1^) at 25°C for 3 days.
Gently knock the bottom of the Erlenmeyer flasks and loosen the medium.
Use forceps to gently pull out the plants from the Erlenmeyer flasks.
Wash off the medium with running tap water gently.
Fill pots with wet compost mixture.
Make a hole in the compost and place the regenerated plants into it.
Compact the soil around the plants and water slightly.
Cover the plants with zip bags and secure them to the pot using rubber bands.
Incubate under light conditions gradually increasing from 300 μmol m^-2^ s^-1^ to 500 μmol m^-2^ s^-1^, at 16 hours of light per day, at 25°C/18°C for 1-2 weeks.
Add water into the tray under pots when soil is dry.
Remove zip bags after plants are in good condition.
Water plants when soil is getting dry.
Incubate under constant light (500 μmol m^-2^ s^-1^, 16 hours of light per day) at 25°C/18°C for 1-2 weeks.
Number the regeneration cucumber plants.
Cut a piece of mature leaf from each plant.
Extract genome DNA using the cetyltrimethy ammonium bromide (CTAB) method.
Confirm transgenic plants have been inserted with T-DNA using specific primers designed on the T-DNA.
Perform PCR amplification.
Conduct gel electrophoresis assay.
Transfer molecularly identified transgenic plants to greenhouse.
Maintain temperature between 16°C and 33°C in the greenhouse.
Set light intensity at 500 μmol m^-2 s^-1.
Keep relative humidity between 70% and 80%.
Clip female and male flowers on the same plant the day before blooming.
Perform artificial self-pollination using the same plant's male flowers to female flowers in the morning after clipping.
Clip female flowers post-pollination to prevent pollen from other plants.
Wait until the epidermis of autochory fruits turns yellow, indicating seed maturity.
Harvest seeds when they are fully mature.
Place harvested seeds under cool and dry conditions for 1-2 weeks.
Open cucumber fruit using a knife to collect seeds.
Wash collected seeds with tap water.
Store washed seeds in mesh bags under cool and dry conditions until completely dried.
Germinate T0 transgenic cucumber seeds directly in soil or in cultivation containers filled with soil.
Use germinated seeds for further analysis of gene biology after identifying T-DNA insertion.
Refer to Step 25 and Step 26 for T-DNA identification.
